newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom-SinTel rumours swamp Jakarta market.
newsitem.headline: Telkom-SinTel rumours swamp Jakarta market.

text.p: Rumours of a link-up between PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) and Singapore Telecom and a possible listing of Telkom's cellular unit swamped the Jakarta stock market on Thursday, analysts said.

Although a Telkom official denied market rumours that Singapore Telecom had bought a share in the Indonesian firm, the talk triggered off a wave of blue-chip buying which lasted through the day. Telkom, also listed in New York, closed 150 rupiah up at 4,050.
Singapore Telecom said it would not comment on the rumours.

"There seem to be no major fundamental surprises. Telkom's strong showing on the stock market is partly due to rumours," said Agung Prabowo, a telecommunications analyst with large local state-owned brokerage firm Danareksa Sekuritas.
"From the company's side, we have no plan to sell a stake to Singapore Telecom," Thomas Widjanarto, the head of Telkom's investor relations unit, told Reuters.
There was also market talk of a possible private placement, analysts and brokers said.
They said Telkom's subsidiary cellular operator PT Telkomsel was likely to float shares later this year or early next year.
Telkom will announce its first quarter earnings on Friday and is likely to post a positive result, but the market was focusing on the rumours, brokers said.
Telkom was expected in the first quarter of this year a net profit of around 450 billion rupiah, around a quarter of an expected 1.8 trillion rupiah full year figure, Prabowo said.
Telkom posted a net profit of 307 billion rupiah in the first quarter of 1996 and 1.5 trillion rupiah in the full year.

Another analyst who asked not to be named said he did not expect any surprises in the first quarter results, saying fundamentals such as the amount of additional lines in service and line usages were likely to be within expectations.
The analyst declined to reveal his forecast for first quarter earnings but said he expected Telkom's full year net profit also at around 1.8 trillion rupiah.

"I expect Telkom shares to reach the 4,500 rupiah level at the end of the year due to strong fundamentals and expected active foreign buying after the election is over," Laksono Widodo, a telecommunications analyst with ING Barings Indonesia, said.
Foreign investors were underweight on Indonesia lately because of the election, but when the poll was over they would be buying liquid big-capitalised stocks, Widodo added.
"Most of the stocks that have made strong gains today are the liquid big-caps which are usually the first to attract foreign investors," Widodo said.
The Jakarta composite index rose 17.00 points, or 2.53 percent to close at 689.50 points on Thursday.
